issues.description: signing_mode_enum module-level function complects two unrelated mode derivations under one name
issues.detail: There is now a property VerifySignature.signing_mode_enum (parses a string) and a module-level signing_mode_enum(request) (derives mode from is_hex/safe_mode booleans). Same name, different inputs, different semantics. That is exactly the kind of incidental complecting decomposition is supposed to remove. Rename one (e.g. derive_signing_mode_from_flags) so the value being computed is named for what it is, not where it is called.

issues.description: verify_signature still complects pure verification with address/puzzle-hash binding check
issues.detail: The new util takes a signing_mode + key + message + signature (a pure cryptographic question) and an optional address (an identity-binding question) and returns one VerifySignatureResponse that conflates both failure modes behind a single isValid bool plus an error string. These are two values: signature_valid and address_matches. Decompose into two small functions and let the caller compose; the RPC layer can assemble the response object.

issues.description: sign_message message-encoding branch is duplicated between sign_message and verify_signature
issues.detail: Both functions re-implement the same SigningMode -> bytes mapping with slightly different branch ordering and a hex vs utf8 default. That mapping is a value (mode -> encoder) and should live in one place as a pure function, e.g. message_bytes_for_mode(mode, message). Right now the two copies can drift, and one already disagrees on the default branch, which is exactly the kind of bug that decomplection prevents.

issues.description: SignMessageResponse field named pubkey alongside a function parameter named public_key is gratuitous renaming
issues.detail: Inside sign_message the local is public_key, then it is stored as pubkey in the response dataclass, while VerifySignatureResponse and other types use their own conventions. Same value, three names across one small module. Pick one name for the value (public_key) and use it everywhere; abbreviations like pubkey buy nothing and cost grep-ability.

issues.description: verify_signature docstring is a stale OO-style stub referring to a non-existent request object
issues.detail: The function takes explicit keyword args, but the docstring says ':param request:' and ':return:' with no content. This is residue from a prior shape where everything was bundled into a request object. Either delete the stub or describe the actual values flowing in and out; a wrong docstring is worse than none.

issues.description: test_sign_message_by_nft_id repeats the same verify-against-mode block four times instead of table-driving the cases
issues.detail: The new test is four near-identical blocks varying only (is_hex, safe_mode, expected encoder). That is the SigningMode -> encoder table again, this time in test form. Parametrize over a list of (is_hex, safe_mode, encode_fn) tuples; the test becomes one block and the table of cases becomes data you can read at a glance.

review.summary: The extraction is a real improvement: pulling sign_message off three wallet classes and exposing current_p2_puzzle_hash decomposes value (the bytes to sign) from identity (which wallet's key). But the new util still complects two concerns inside verify_signature (cryptographic validity and address binding) and the SigningMode -> bytes encoding table is duplicated across sign_message and verify_signature, with the encoder mapping also re-encoded a third time in the new tests. There is also a naming collision: VerifySignature.signing_mode_enum (parse a string) and a module-level signing_mode_enum(request) (derive from booleans) are two different values sharing one name. Decompose the encoder table into a single pure function, split signature-valid from address-matches, and rename one of the two signing_mode_enum surfaces. No P0s; structure is healthier than before, just not yet simple.
